server.name: community-rpgmaker-mz
server.version: rpgmaker-mz-mcp (npm latest at image build time)
server.note: Drawn in frame order from block 3 of Frame 3. One hundred and twenty eight tools, none of them annotated, editing a game project's JSON data files in place. It refuses to work until a project is selected, and recognises a project by a marker file beside a data directory.
server.note_prelude: Every fixture needs the project selected first, and the selection is session state rather than a file, so it belongs in the server prelude. It calls a different tool from any fixture here, so it takes no fault: the rule that a prelude must not call the tool under test is satisfied and enforced by the spec loader.
server.note_observer: The effect is a rewritten JSON data file, so the plain filesystem observer is canonical and no projection is needed: the records carry no timestamps and the identifiers the server assigns are sequential rather than random.
server.note_probes: Each fixture probes the matching search tool with the argument name that tool actually declares. The first attempt passed `query`, which the server rejected as an unknown argument, and both rows then came back unconfirmable. That would have been a finding about the server when it was a mistake in the spec, and it would have moved the pooled unconfirmable rate in this study's favour, so the probe is checked against the schema rather than guessed.

fixtures.note: An append into a JSON array with no key in the arguments: the server assigns the identifier, so the caller has nothing to collapse a repeat onto. The duplicate-prone shape, in a file a person edits by hand in a game editor.
The same shape on a second data file, included because the two write different files and a fault that lands between them is the partial-outcome case the task clusters are built around.
